Owner decided to remove the article and let /blog/compress-mp4-webm-video-in-browser return 404 rather than write a replacement or redirect. Verified first that the URL returned 200 and was in the live sitemap.xml, and that no live page compresses video: LIVE_TOOL_ROUTES has no /video/* route and no operation id in lib/tools/** matches video; the gzip compressor's own notice says it is not a media-specific optimizer. A redirect to the image-compression article would be a soft 404 on a mismatched topic. The exclusion is documented in removed-tool-redirects.ts and locked by a test asserting the path stays unredirected and no blog post publishes the slug; the test was confirmed to fail when the redirect is added back. C3. Node QC proves operation logic but not that a browser can run it, so the operations are now bundled and executed inside Chromium and WebKit against the same output contract, and the image editor and PDF page tools are driven through their real UI. All 615 operations and all 13 UI destinations pass in both engines: no tool needed removing. Three real problems were found and fixed: the e2e suite had been attaching to another project's dev server on port 3000, so all 628 route smoke tests were passing against an unrelated app (now its own port, production build, plus a global setup that refuses a foreign server); WebKit returns a PNG for a canvas WebP request, which the image editor and optimizer treated as failure, leaving both dead on that engine at their default WebP setting (they now keep the produced blob, name the file for its real format and show it on the receipt); and two legacy specs fed the AI background remover a flat single-colour square with no subject, which the model correctly refused.
